newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW -French June consumer spending down.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -French June consumer spending down.

text.p: Following are reactions from economists to the 2.9 percent fall in June consumer spending after a revised 0.5 percent fall in May, as reported by national statistics institute INSEE.

The numbers are not good. We were expecting a one percent drop. I think it's a combination of things. There was an unfavourable number of Saturdays and bad weather hurt clothing, and sales started late. All these contributed to the fall but the drop is due to more than exceptional factors. Is it it threat to recovery? -- we don't think so, though consumption is a weak link in the chain. The early indications for July are, however, for a strong month.
STUART THOMSON, ECONOMIST, CREDIT AGRICOLE INDOSUEZ

We had been looking for a fall of one percent after a 1.1 drop in May but we've had a revision to 0.5. But take 0.6 off and it's still 2.3 percent, more than half our forecast. It shows household consumption has fallen in the second quarter and that gives a slow start to the year.

June was a very poor month weather-wise and we have the same car effect that we have seen continually this year. Taking into account the bad weather and the working days factors means it is clearly not as bad as it first appears, and we should see a rebound in July and August.
But the problem is political as (the government) will have to base its tax estimates (for the 1998 budget) on these figures.

The government desire for a consumer-led recovery has certainly been dented and it does make its task of reaching three percent (deficit as percentage of GDP) next year more difficult. We've seen money being raised from the corporate sector and in order to raise extra money next year the government is really having to look towards the consumer.
This drop is stronger than expected. I was expecting (a drop of) 0.7 to 1.0 percent.
But we had to expect a bad number because car sales were bad in June and department store sales were down.

Cars were at their lowest for a long time as a proportion of the overall figure and we may see a mechanical rebound in July. Also the (summer) sales have apparently been quite good. Maybe July will completely compensate for June.
